Commentary.Commentary: Right then! we are all set and the players and the Umpires are on the field to start the run chase. It's Hayley Matthews and Qiana Joseph are the opening batters for the West Indies Women. Renuka Singh Thakur, fresh from a FIFER has the new ball in hand for India Women. Let's Play!
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Jemimah Rodrigues, the Indian batter, expresses her joy in contributing to the team's success, emphasizing the importance of scoring runs quickly rather than focusing solely on milestones. She praises Harleen Deol for her inspiring comeback with a century after ACL surgery, calling it an emotional moment. She also commends Pratika Rawal's performance, noting her composure in her second game, and highlights the team's improved batting efforts as they continue to raise their standards.

In contrast, the bowling from the visiting team has been lackluster. They've struggled to contain the flow of runs, and their fielders haven't helped matters either. Misfields have added to the bowlers' woes, making it difficult for them to put any pressure on the Indian batters. As a result, India has been able to dictate the terms of the game. Afy Fletcher, Deandra Dottin, Zaida James and Qiana Joseph took one each while Karishma Ramharack went wicketless but bowled the best amongst the visitors. The target is mammoth and the chances of West Indies Women chasing this down look slim but we never know what we have in offer from the Women in Maroon. Hayley Matthews and Deandra Dottin hold the key to any sort of hope for the visitors. We will be back in some time with the chase.

The Indian innings got off to a solid start, courtesy of a fine partnership between Smriti Mandhana and Pratika Rawal. Both openers were scoring freely, but an unfortunate mix-up in the middle led to a break in the partnership. However, Harleen Deol took over, scoring a brilliant maiden century to keep the momentum going. What's been impressive about India's batting display is that every batter apart from Kaur, made a useful contribution to the team's cause. At one point, it seemed like India might even breach the 400-run mark, such was their dominance. The Indian batters have been clinical in their approach, making the most of every scoring opportunity. Smriti Mandhana, Pratika Rawal, and Jemimah Rodrigues scored half-centuries each while Harleen Deol went a step ahead and smashed a ton.
We've reached the midway break in this contest, and Indian skipper Harmanpreet Kaur must be thrilled with her team's batting display. India has posted an impressive total of 358 on the board.
